chapter: Reel IV retellings and New York pianists
title: Josephine Baker from Boston chorus girl to Paris
summary: Whaley played piano in Joe Jordan's band for a film with Josephine Baker, and visited her in Paris in 1966 with Duke.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Piano player -- director of the band. He had the band all down at some theatre on 46th Street. I played the piano and he had a band made a movie picture with Josephine Baker, and he was the director, and I was the piano player. Josephine Baker did -- did I tell you about her?
No, go on, let's hear about that, Tom.
Well, Josephine Baker was a chorus girl in line up in Boston, see?

And she got out of line dancing, and did a chorus all by herself, and the guy told her to keep it in. Now, she came to New York, and the first thing I know she's over in Europe dancing with the bananas. After ...
Bananas. They used to call her The Banana Girl, dancing with a bunch of bananas, nude like.
And Josephine, she was very nice. When I went over there, she entertained me like I was royalty.
: When did you go over there, Tom?
I went over there in -- I think it was in '66.
And I went to see Josephine, and she was in Paris, and I went by and saw her, and when she came over here, Ruth Ellington had a party for her.
Yeah. And Josephine came over and spoke to me, and says, told me to keep my chin up. And she left and that's the last time I saw her -- she died, and that was one great girl.
